Website is a web-based application developed using PHP and MySQL to provide users with a convenient and efficient platform for purchasing apparel from anywhere at any time. The system allows customers to browse products by category, view detailed descriptions, manage shopping carts, and place secure orders. It enhances the traditional shopping experience by offering quick search, user authentication, and easy navigation through a responsive interface.

For administrators, the system simplifies store management by providing modules to manage inventory, update product details, monitor stock availability, and handle customer orders in real time. By adopting a centralized approach, the platform improves business operations, reduces manual effort, and supports future scalability. This project aims to deliver a reliable, user-friendly, and cost-effective e-commerce solution tailored for the clothing retail industry.

The System Study is a critical component of the project lifecycle, aimed at understanding the existing environment, identifying challenges, and assessing the scope and feasibility of the proposed system. In this case, the Online Clothing Store project was planned after a detailed study of the traditional clothing retail business, its limitations, and the potential improvements that an online platform could offer.

The System Study forms the foundation of the software development process. It involves understanding the problem domain, identifying user needs, and analyzing how a new system can fulfill those needs effectively. For this project, the system study helps in identifying the issues faced by both customers and store owners in the traditional apparel shopping process.
Traditional cloth retail systems, which depend heavily on physical infrastructure and manual processes, come with various limitations:
1. Limited Size Availability: Not all cloth sizes may be available, leading to customer frustration.
2. Inaccurate Product Images/Descriptions: Misleading photos or incomplete descriptions can cause returns.
3. Return/Exchange Issues: Complicated return policies can frustrate customers.
4. Fake Reviews or Ratings: Misleading reviews reduce customer trust.
5. Ineffective Search & Filters: Hard for customers to find the right cloth quickly.
6. Inventory Mismatch: Product may show as available online but is out of stock in reality

The feasibility study is essential in evaluating whether the proposed system is practical, sustainable, and worth implementing. The Online cloth Store project was evaluated on the following feasibility factors:
- The system uses PHP, MySQL, JavaScript, and Bootstrap — all of which are widely supported and open-source technologies.
- Hosting is compatible with most standard Linux-based servers.
- Basic system requirements for the customer include only a browser and internet connection.
- The system is easy to use and requires minimal training for both customers and admins.
- Customer workflows (like login, shopping, and checkout) are intuitive.
- Admin interfaces allow straightforward management of products, users, and transactions
- Development costs are low due to the use of open-source technologies.
- No need for physical infrastructure reduces initial capital investment.
- Long-term maintenance is affordable and scalable.
- Secure login and encrypted data handling ensure user privacy.
- Terms and conditions, as well as privacy policies, are clearly defined for legal compliance.
Functional requirements define the core features and operations of the system. These are the functionalities that the system must perform:
- Customers must be able to create an account with personal information like name, email, address, and password.
- The system should verify credentials during login and manage user sessions securely.
- Users can view product listings categorized by type (men, women, kids featured, etc.).
- Each product page will display the image, description, price, size, and availability
- Customers can add, remove, or update quantities of products in their cart.
- The cart should persist across sessions until checkout.
- Customers can proceed to checkout, confirm shipping details, and complete payment.
- The system will generate an order confirmation and unique order ID.
- Admins can add, update, and delete products from the inventory.
- Admins can mark products as “featured” or categorize them
- Users can search for products by name, price range, or size.
- Filters should dynamically adjust the product list
- Users and admins must be able to log out securely
These are performance-related specifications that define how well the system performs:
- The interface must be simple and intuitive for non-technical users.
- Navigation should be responsive and user-friendly.
- User passwords should be stored securely (hashed and encrypted)
- Data protection measures must be in place for transactions and personal information.
- Pages should load in under 2 seconds on average.
- The system should support multiple users simultaneously (scalability).
- The system should be available 99.9% of the time, with minimal downtime.
- Code should be well-documented and modular for easy updates and debugging.
- The system should run on major web browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Edge).
- Mobile responsiveness should be maintained via Bootstrap
